text:
ellie: Heads-up — ACME reported elevated latency + intermittent 401s for EU users since ~02:00 UTC. All traffic supposed to land in eu-west1 but traces show tokens being validated in ap-southeast. :rotating_light:
ian_sre: Can you paste a trace id or request_id?
ellie: rq_2026-03-16_9ab12c. From their logs: backend region header is ap-sg-1 and we see 401s followed by billing hits.
maya_pd: Do we have any recent GeoIP or CDN edge deploys? I remember a GeoDB refresh landed last night.
sam_ops: GeoIP refresh did go out at 01:30 but the rollout was staged. No infra deploys otherwise.
ian_sre: Running a few spot checks — seems some resolvers in their ISP are returning old anycast answers pointing to global gateway IPs. Could be caching at ISP level + our CDN returning mixed views.
ellie: Customer provided a dig from one of their users (Singapore office). Snippet:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> api.redwood.example.com
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.example.com. 3600 IN CNAME global-gw-1.example.cdn.
global-gw-1.example.cdn. 21600 IN A 203.0.113.45
```
They expected an EU IP.
maya_pd: That A record TTL is big (21600). If upstream CDN backfilled a global gw, ISP caches will hold it for hours.
sam_ops: Also seeing EDNS-client-subnet being stripped by some resolvers — removes our ability to geo-route.
ian_sre: Repro steps I used:
1) dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example.com -> 203.0.113.45
2) curl -v --resolve 'api.redwood.example.com:443:203.0.113.45' https://api.redwood.example.com/health -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
Response had X-Redwood-Region: ap-sg-1 and 401 for that token (token scoped to eu).
ellie: Customer saw billing spikes because their token got routed to wrong tenant scope and hit auth fallback.
maya_pd: Short-term mitigation: reduce CNAME/A TTLs on global gateways to 60s and push small rollback of GeoDB sync to ensure eu edges are returned. Can we do that quickly?
sam_ops: I can push TTL change for the global-gw records but need approval to touch DNS zone.
ian_sre: Also recommend a temporary policy: prefer region hint header when present to avoid auth fallout: honor X-Client-Region header for 30m for affected orgs. That avoids reissuing tokens.
ellie: I've told ACME to have their users flush local DNS / restart browsers; asked them to test with 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8. They pushed back — want us to fix server-side.
sam_ops: TTL change pushed (global-gw A/CNAME -> 60s). Propagation should start within a minute but ISPs may respect old TTL.
deploy-bot: geoip-db-sync rollback initiated by @sam_ops at 02:45 UTC — job id job_4598.
ian_sre: I'm running active probes from EU nodes to check where answers land. Will post probe matrix shortly.
maya_pd: Good, also file a support escalation to accounts for the billing impact (JP invoice). Ellie, include usage delta and affected window.
ellie: On it. Escalation email drafted. Also collecting request_ids for replay debugging.
ian_sre: Probe update: eu-probe1 -> eu IP ok, eu-probe2 (ISP X) -> global gw IP. Looks like a resolver cohort in ISP X caching old view.
sam_ops: Forcing fallback mapping for ACME org to eu-edge via route override until their caches expire. Will monitor 10m.
ellie: ACME just confirmed a user in Amsterdam can authenticate again. They say latency back to normal. :thumbsup:
maya_pd: Postmortem action items: 1) reduce default global gateway TTLs during GeoDB rollouts, 2) add monitoring for resolver cohorts that strip ECS/EDNS, 3) add per-org regional override option in console.
ian_sre: Agree. I'll open incident-PR and link traces.
ellie: Thanks team — I'll update ACME and close after 1h stable.
